title: CollisionShape3D with shape ConcavePolygonShape3D and other settings default creates error in Editor output probably because there are no vertices and no clear way to add them in the inspector
body: ### Tested versions 4.4.1 stable ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900HX (32 threads) ### Issue description Adding a CollisionShape3D as a child of a StaticBody3D and setting the "shape" resource to a new ConcavePolygonShape3D creates the following errors (not warnings) in the Editor's output: ``` ERROR: servers/rendering_server.cpp:1193 - Condition "array_len == 0" is true. Returning: ERR_INVALID_DATA ERROR: scene/resources/mesh.cpp:1810 - Condition "err != OK" is true. ``` You can see the minimum setup I used to produce this in a brand-new project in the attached screenshot: The primary issues I see with this are that(a) this is fairly cryptic to someone who may not understand why the rendering server and mesh class are even involved here at all, which makes debugging more difficult than it needs to be and (b) this is a very "default" case, and in some situations a collision shape with empty geometry may actually be necessary or at least difficult to avoid, for example when the actual geometry will be created procedurally at run-time, so this case should _not_ be causing errors in the project. Side note: Turning the "Debug Fill" boolean option to FALSE (which is not the default) in the CollisionShape3D prevents this error from appearing. This is especially puzzling because my understanding was that the "Debug > Visible Collision Shapes" option didn't work in the editor anyway, only running projects. ### Steps to reproduce See the above screenshot. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [bug-test-project - Copy.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21585912/bug-test-project.-.Copy.zip)
